title: [Re] Graph Edit Networks

en.text: A quiet but practical problem in graph machine learning is predicting how a graph changes over time. Given a sequence of graphs that evolves step by step, you want to forecast the next one — and not just as a label, but as the specific set of structural changes that turn the current graph into the next: insert a node, delete an edge, relabel a vertex.

Standard graph neural networks are an awkward fit for this. They emit probability scores over nodes or edges, not the discrete structural operations that actually transform one graph into another. Graph Edit Networks (GEN) were proposed to close that gap: an output layer that sits on top of a GNN and predicts an explicit, human-readable edit script instead of a score.

This post is not about the original GEN paper but about an independent reproduction of it. The authors re-implement GEN from scratch, check each of the paper's four experimental claims one by one, and — crucially — write down the synthetic data generators that the original paper described only in passing. The verdict is mixed: three of the four claims survive, but the claim that backward passes scale linearly does not. More pointedly, the reproduction finds that several of the benchmarks reward a model for revisiting transformations it has already seen, rather than for genuinely generalizing.

en.caption: Figure 1. Three cyclical time series produced by the Edit Cycles data generator. Each transition is written as an edit operation δ — ins to insert a node, eins to insert an edge, del to delete a node — and each red arrow is a single graph edit. This is exactly what GEN learns to predict: not a static graph, but the script of operations that maps the current graph to the next.

en.text: Paper: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.6574701 (ReScience C 2022, ML Reproducibility Challenge 2021)
Code: https://github.com/MarusaOrazem/reproducibility_challenge
The problem: predicting how a graph changes, not what it is

Many real systems are graphs that move: molecules break and form bonds during a reaction, ties in a social network come and go, a logical expression gets rewritten as it is simplified. To predict their next state, a model needs to output a set of structural edits, not a heatmap of node or edge probabilities. Forcing 'the next graph' into a node-or-edge scoring framework tends to be both unintuitive and hard for a human to interpret afterwards.

GEN changes the prediction target to the edit script itself. It assumes graph evolution is Markovian: the next graph depends only on the current one. The model therefore only has to predict a finite string of edits for the current graph, which — applied in order — yields the next graph.
The method: turning a prediction into a sequence of graph edits

GEN attaches to a standard GNN backbone, and instead of scores it emits an edit script drawn from a small vocabulary of operations: insert, delete, or replace a node, and insert or delete an edge. Applying that script in sequence to the current graph produces the next one — precisely the Markovian assumption the method rests on.

The training signal comes from reference mappings between time-adjacent graphs. Those mappings are obtained with graph-edit-distance (GED) approximators, because computing the exact distance is NP-hard, and are then converted into a per-node teaching signal. The reproduction trains two loss variants — an adapted hinge loss and an adapted cross-entropy loss — and, for large citation graphs, adds edge-filtering schemes that cap how many edge edits each node may propose. The baseline is a modified Variational Graph Autoencoder (VGAE).

en.caption: Figure 2. One tree evolution from the Boolean Formulae generator: the leftmost graph is the syntax tree of the logical formula (x∨(y∧¬y))∨x, and each subsequent step is a logical simplification of the previous graph. Each δ box lists the edits for that step (del to delete, repl to replace). GEN's job is to predict such a script given the current tree.

en.text: What the reproduction did: rewrite the code, document the data, change the protocol

The value here goes well beyond re-running the numbers. The authors re-implement GEN in Python, check that the code matches the method as described (fixing a section of the original authors' code along the way), and thoroughly document the five synthetic data-generating processes (DGPs) that the original paper only sketched. The five fall into two families: dynamical graph systems — Edit Cycles, Degree Rules, and a Conway's Game of Life process — and tree dynamical systems — Boolean Formulae and Peano Addition. Scaling is tested on the arXiv HEP-Th citation network of roughly 27,700 papers, from which a rolling time window carves out 1,554 sub-graphs with node counts N_G ∈ [100, 2786].

They also flag a hazard in the original setup: training and test series can overlap, giving the model the chance to be evaluated on transitions it saw during training. To address it, the authors propose a stricter risk-estimation protocol that holds out 100 graphs as an independent test set, and re-run the experiments under it.
Results: three of four claims stand, one falls

The original paper makes four core claims: (i) GEN beats VGAE on all three dynamical graph DGPs; (ii) it reaches near-perfect accuracy on the tree DGPs; (iii) forward passes scale sub-quadratically with graph size; and (iv) backward passes scale linearly. The reproduction confirms the first three and refutes the fourth.

The decisive evidence is the slope of a log-log fit of runtime against graph size (a slope below 2 is sub-quadratic; a slope of 1 is linear). Forward-pass slopes come in clearly below 2, so sub-quadratic scaling holds. But the backward-pass slopes, under both edge-filtering schemes, sit clearly above 1 — that is, super-linear. They remain sub-quadratic, but they are not the linear growth the original paper reported.

en.caption: Figure 3. Runtime versus graph scale (x-axis: node count from 100 to 3k; y-axis: runtime; both log-scaled). The four panels show forward and backward passes under Flexible and Constant edge filtering. The black line is the fitted trend: forward passes stay shallow and sub-quadratic, while backward passes rise noticeably faster — especially Constant.backward (bottom right), whose slope is well above 1, directly contradicting the linear-scaling claim.

Table 1. Slopes of the log-log runtime fit (mean ± standard deviation over 5 repetitions). A slope < 2 is sub-quadratic; = 1 is linear. Forward passes are sub-quadratic; backward passes are all above 1 — super-linear — which refutes the original linear-scaling claim.

en.text: Fidelity of the reproduction: the numbers largely match

On accuracy, the reproduction is reassuring: the vast majority of metrics fall within one standard deviation of the originally reported values. The largest deviation was an increase in VGAE deletion precision and insertion recall on the Edit Cycles task, which did not overturn GEN's overall win. On the tree tasks, Boolean Formulae accuracy is 0.98 ± 0.02, and Peano Addition is a perfect 1.0.

en.caption: Figure 4. A diagnostic δ-boxplot: the y-axis is (reproduction − reported), with the red dashed line at 0 marking perfect agreement. These results are for the Game of Life DGP with the hinge-loss GEN under the stricter risk-estimation protocol and a larger test set. Most boxes hug 0, with deviations within about 0.05 — the reproduction closely tracks the original.

en.text: The authors run two robustness checks. First, they replace the ad-hoc random-graph initialization with the established Erdős–Rényi and Configuration models; every metric moves by less than 0.05. Second, introducing the 100-graph held-out test set shifts scores only slightly, by δ ∈ [−0.1, 0.05]. Both point to the same conclusion: the original results do not hinge on an experimental shortcut.
The sharper question: are these benchmarks actually hard?

The most interesting result is the last diagnostic. When the authors sample from the tree generators to see what sequences they actually produce, they find a problem: the generators overwhelmingly produce trees that cannot be simplified at all. Across more than 300,000 samples, the probability of drawing a simplifiable tree is only 0.13 ± 0.003 for Boolean Formulae and 0.26 ± 0.002 for Peano Addition.

en.caption: Figure 5. Distribution of sampled time-series lengths from the tree DGPs (boolean and peano; rows correspond to a maximum of 3–5 operations). The mass piles up at very short series: a large share of samples have almost no simplification steps to perform. That undercuts how demanding the near-perfect-accuracy tasks really are.

en.text: This puts an asterisk on the tidy 'near-perfect accuracy' numbers on the tree tasks. If most test samples require no simplification in the first place, high accuracy reflects an easy task more than a strongly expressive model. Put differently, the model may be replaying transformations it has already learned rather than generalizing to new ones.
Takeaway: elegant and reproducible, but don't overrate its scaling or its difficulty

Taken together, the reproduction offers a measured verdict. GEN is an elegant, interpretable, and genuinely reproducible architecture, and three of the paper's four claims survive independent scrutiny. But the reproduction corrects one scaling claim — backward passes are super-linear, not linear — and it cautions that several of the synthetic benchmarks let the model win by revisiting transitions it has already learned rather than by generalizing.

It is worth noting that the study's careful documentation of the five data generators may be as valuable as its verdict on the claims: anyone reusing these benchmarks benefits directly from it. The authors close with a call for more rigorous, more practically grounded evaluation of an otherwise promising architecture.

zh.text: 在图神经网络（Graph Neural Network, GNN）里，一个不太起眼但很实际的任务是「图的时间序列预测」：给定一个随时间演化的图序列，预测下一时刻的图长什么样。它不是给节点或边打个分那么简单，而是要说清楚从当前图到下一张图，具体发生了哪些结构变化。
标准 GNN 在这里有点力不从心。它们输出的是节点或边的概率分数，而不是「插入一个节点、删掉一条边、给某个顶点改标签」这种能真正把一张图变成下一张图的结构化操作。Graph Edit Network（GEN，图编辑网络）就是为填这个缺口而提出的：它作为 GNN 的输出层，直接预测一段可读的「编辑脚本」。
本文要讲的不是 GEN 原始论文，而是一篇独立复现研究。作者重新实现了 GEN，逐一核对了原文的四个实验主张，并把原论文语焉不详的几个合成数据生成器彻底写清楚。结论是有褒有贬：四个主张里三个站得住，但「反向传播随图规模线性扩展」这一条被推翻了；更尖锐的是，他们发现有几个 benchmark 其实是在奖励模型「记住见过的变换」，而不是真正的泛化能力。

zh.caption: 图1 Edit Cycles 数据生成器产生的三条循环时间序列。每一步的图变换都被写成一段编辑操作 δ（如 ins 插入节点、eins 插入边、del 删除节点），红色箭头即一次「图编辑」。这正是 GEN 要学着预测的目标：不是一张静态图，而是把当前图变成下一张图的那串操作。

zh.text: 论文：https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.6574701 （ReScience C 2022，ML Reproducibility Challenge 2021）
代码：https://github.com/MarusaOrazem/reproducibility_challenge
问题：预测「图怎么变」，而不是「图是什么」
很多真实系统本身就是一张会变的图：分子在反应中断键成键、社交网络里关系此消彼长、逻辑表达式在化简中不断改写。想预测它们的下一步，模型需要输出的是一组结构编辑，而不是一张概率热力图。把「下一张图」硬塞进节点/边打分的框架里，往往既不直观也不好解释。
GEN 的思路是把预测目标换成「编辑脚本」本身。它假设图的演化是马尔可夫式的：下一张图只由当前图决定。于是模型只需为当前图预测一串有限的编辑操作，依次执行后就得到下一张图。
方法：GEN 如何把预测变成一串「图编辑」
GEN 接在一个标准 GNN 主干之后，输出的不再是分数，而是一段编辑脚本。脚本由一套很小的操作词汇构成：插入 / 删除 / 替换一个节点，插入 / 删除一条边。把这串操作按顺序作用到当前图上，就得到下一张图，这正对应它所依赖的马尔可夫假设。

训练信号来自相邻时刻两张图之间的「参考映射」。这些映射通过图编辑距离（Graph Edit Distance, GED）的近似算法得到，因为精确计算 GED 是 NP-hard 的；再把映射转成每个节点的教学信号。复现中训练了两种损失变体（改写的 hinge loss 与 cross-entropy loss），并为大规模引文图额外加了「边过滤」机制，限制每个节点能提出多少条边编辑。对照的 baseline 是一个改造过的变分图自编码器（Variational Graph Autoencoder, VGAE）。

zh.caption: 图2 一次树结构的演化，采样自 Boolean Formulae 生成器：最左侧是逻辑公式 (x∨(y∧¬y))∨x 对应的语法树，之后每一步都是对上一张图的一次逻辑化简。每个 δ 方框列出该步要执行的编辑操作（del 删除、repl 替换）。GEN 要学的就是在给定当前树时预测出这样一段脚本。

zh.text: 复现做了什么：重写代码、写清数据、换一套评测协议

这篇复现的价值不只是「跑一遍看数字对不对」。作者用 Python 重新实现了 GEN，核对代码与原文方法是否一致（过程中还帮原作者修好了一段代码），并把原论文只是一笔带过的五个合成数据生成器（DGP）逐一写清楚。这五个 DGP 分两类：动态图系统 Edit Cycles、Degree Rules、Game of Life，以及树结构动态系统 Boolean Formulae、Peano Addition。扩展性实验则用了 arXiv HEP-Th 引文网络（约 27,700 篇论文），从中用滚动时间窗切出 1554 个子图，节点数 N_G ∈ [100, 2786]。
他们还指出原实验一个隐患：训练和测试可能落在同一批图上，模型有机会在评测时「重逢」训练时见过的变换。为此作者提出一套更严格的风险估计协议，专门留出 100 张图作为独立测试集，并在这套协议下重跑实验。
结果：四个主张，三个成立，一个被推翻
原论文有四个核心主张：(i) GEN 在三个动态图 DGP 上都胜过 VGAE；(ii) 在树结构 DGP 上达到近乎完美的准确率；(iii) 前向传播随图规模呈亚二次（sub-quadratic）扩展；(iv) 反向传播随图规模线性扩展。复现证实了前三个，但推翻了第四个。
关键证据是运行时间随图规模的对数-对数拟合斜率（斜率小于 2 即亚二次，等于 1 即线性）。前向传播的斜率确实明显小于 2，亚二次成立；但反向传播在两种边过滤方案下的斜率都明显大于 1，也就是超线性（super-linear）。它仍然是亚二次的，但绝不是原文所说的线性。

zh.caption: 图3 运行时间与图规模的关系（横轴节点数 100→3k，纵轴运行时间，均为对数刻度）。四个子图分别是 Flexible / Constant 两种边过滤下的前向（forward）与反向（backward）传播。黑线是拟合趋势：前向平缓、亚二次；反向明显更陡，尤其是右下角 Constant.backward，斜率远大于 1，直接否定了「反向传播线性扩展」的说法。
表1 运行时间对数-对数拟合斜率（5 次重复的均值 ± 标准差）。斜率 <2 为亚二次，=1 为线性。行是两种边过滤方案（Flexible / Constant），列是前向（Forward）与反向（Backward）传播。前向亚二次成立；反向全部大于 1，即超线性，推翻原文的线性主张。

zh.text: 复现的保真度：数字基本对得上
在准确性这一面，复现结果整体令人放心：绝大多数指标都落在原文报告值的一个标准差之内。偏差最大的一处，是 VGAE 在 Edit Cycles 任务上的删除精度与插入召回有所上升，但这并没有翻盘 GEN 的整体胜出。树结构任务上，Boolean Formulae 准确率为 0.98 ± 0.02，Peano Addition 更是达到完美的 1.0，两项都与原文报告高度一致。

zh.caption: 图4 诊断用 δ 箱线图：纵轴是「复现值 − 原文报告值」，红色虚线为 0（完全一致）。这是在 Game of Life DGP、hinge-loss 版 GEN、并采用更严格的风险估计协议和更大测试集下得到的。绝大多数箱体都紧贴 0 附近、偏差在 0.05 以内，说明复现与原文高度吻合。

zh.text: 作者还做了两项稳健性检查。其一，把原实验里随手写的随机图初始化换成成熟的 Erdős–Rényi 模型和 Configuration 模型，所有指标变化都在 0.05 以内。其二，引入前面说的 100 张图独立测试集后，分数只轻微下移，偏移量 δ ∈ [−0.1, 0.05]。结论都指向：原文结果并不依赖某个实验捷径。
更尖锐的追问：这些 benchmark 真的够难吗
真正有意思的是最后一项诊断。作者去采样这些树结构生成器，看它们到底产出什么样的序列，结果发现一个问题：这些生成器绝大多数时候产出的是根本无法再化简的树。在超过 300,000 次采样中，能采到「可化简树」的概率，Boolean Formulae 只有 0.13 ± 0.003，Peano Addition 也只有 0.26 ± 0.002。

zh.caption: 图5 从树结构 DGP 采样得到的时间序列长度分布（boolean 与 peano，行对应最大操作数 3–5）。可以看到分布严重堆在极短序列一侧：大量样本几乎没有可执行的化简步骤。这意味着「近乎完美准确率」的任务，本身可能就没那么有挑战性。

zh.text: 这一发现给「树任务上近乎完美」的漂亮数字打了个问号：如果大部分测试样本本就无需化简，那高准确率更多反映的是任务偏易，而非模型有多强的表达能力。换句话说，模型可能是在重复它已经学会的变换，而不是在泛化。
小结：优雅可复现，但别高估它的扩展性与难度
综合来看，这篇复现给出的评价是有分寸的。GEN 本身是个优雅、可解释、也确实能复现的架构，原文四个主张里三个经受住了独立检验。但复现纠正了其中一个扩展性结论：反向传播是超线性而非线性；同时提醒大家，几个合成 benchmark 让模型「赢在重逢已学过的变换」，而不是真正泛化。
值得一提的是，这份研究里对五个数据生成器的详尽记录，本身可能和它对主张的裁决一样有价值，任何想复用这些 benchmark 的人都能直接受益。作者最后呼吁：对 GEN 这类有潜力的架构，评测应当更严格、更贴近实际用途。

训练信号来自相邻时刻两张图之间的「参考映射」。这些映射通过图编辑距离（Graph Edit Distance, GED）的近似算法得到，因为精确计算 GED 是 NP-hard 的；再把映射转成每个节点的教学信号。复现中训练了两种损失变体（改写的 hinge loss 与 cross-entropy loss），并为大规模引文图额外加了「边过滤」机制，限制每个节点能提出多少条边编辑。对照的 baseline 是一个改造过的变分图自编码器（Variational Graph Autoencoder, VGAE）。

zh.caption: 图2 一次树结构的演化，采样自 Boolean Formulae 生成器：最左侧是逻辑公式 (x∨(y∧¬y))∨x 对应的语法树，之后每一步都是对上一张图的一次逻辑化简。每个 δ 方框列出该步要执行的编辑操作（del 删除、repl 替换）。GEN 要学的就是在给定当前树时预测出这样一段脚本。

Each transition is written as an edit operation δ — ins to insert a node, eins to insert an edge, del to delete a node — and each red arrow is a single graph edit. zh.text: 小结：优雅可复现，但别高估它的扩展性与难度
综合来看，这篇复现给出的评价是有分寸的。GEN 本身是个优雅、可解释、也确实能复现的架构，原文四个主张里三个经受住了独立检验。但复现纠正了其中一个扩展性结论：反向传播是超线性而非线性；同时提醒大家，几个合成 benchmark 让模型「赢在重逢已学过的变换」，而不是真正泛化。
值得一提的是，这份研究里对五个数据生成器的详尽记录，本身可能和它对主张的裁决一样有价值，任何想复用这些 benchmark 的人都能直接受益。作者最后呼吁：对 GEN 这类有潜力的架构，评测应当更严格、更贴近实际用途。

en.text: Paper: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.6574701 (ReScience C 2022, ML Reproducibility Challenge 2021)
Code: https://github.com/MarusaOrazem/reproducibility_challenge
The method: turning a prediction into a sequence of graph edits

GEN attaches to a standard GNN backbone, and instead of scores it emits an edit script drawn from a small vocabulary of operations: insert, delete, or replace a node, and insert or delete an edge. Applying that script in sequence to the current graph produces the next one — precisely the Markovian assumption the method rests on.

The training signal comes from reference mappings between time-adjacent graphs. Those mappings are obtained with graph-edit-distance (GED) approximators, because computing the exact distance is NP-hard, and are then converted into a per-node teaching signal. The reproduction trains two loss variants — an adapted hinge loss and an adapted cross-entropy loss — and, for large citation graphs, adds edge-filtering schemes that cap how many edge edits each node may propose. The baseline is a modified Variational Graph Autoencoder (VGAE).

en.caption: Figure 2. One tree evolution from the Boolean Formulae generator: the leftmost graph is the syntax tree of the logical formula (x∨(y∧¬y))∨x, and each subsequent step is a logical simplification of the previous graph. Each δ box lists the edits for that step (del to delete, repl to replace). GEN's job is to predict such a script given the current tree.

zh.text: 复现做了什么：重写代码、写清数据、换一套评测协议

这篇复现的价值不只是「跑一遍看数字对不对」。作者用 Python 重新实现了 GEN，核对代码与原文方法是否一致（过程中还帮原作者修好了一段代码），并把原论文只是一笔带过的五个合成数据生成器（DGP）逐一写清楚。这五个 DGP 分两类：动态图系统 Edit Cycles、Degree Rules、Game of Life，以及树结构动态系统 Boolean Formulae、Peano Addition。扩展性实验则用了 arXiv HEP-Th 引文网络（约 27,700 篇论文），从中用滚动时间窗切出 1554 个子图，节点数 N_G ∈ [100, 2786]。

zh.text: 在图神经网络（Graph Neural Network, GNN）里，一个不太起眼但很实际的任务是「图的时间序列预测」：给定一个随时间演化的图序列，预测下一时刻的图长什么样。它不是给节点或边打个分那么简单，而是要说清楚从当前图到下一张图，具体发生了哪些结构变化。
标准 GNN 在这里有点力不从心。它们输出的是节点或边的概率分数，而不是「插入一个节点、删掉一条边、给某个顶点改标签」这种能真正把一张图变成下一张图的结构化操作。Graph Edit Network（GEN，图编辑网络）就是为填这个缺口而提出的：它作为 GNN 的输出层，直接预测一段可读的「编辑脚本」。
本文要讲的不是 GEN 原始论文，而是一篇独立复现研究。作者重新实现了 GEN，逐一核对了原文的四个实验主张，并把原论文语焉不详的几个合成数据生成器彻底写清楚。结论是有褒有贬：四个主张里三个站得住，但「反向传播随图规模线性扩展」这一条被推翻了；更尖锐的是，他们发现有几个 benchmark 其实是在奖励模型「记住见过的变换」，而不是真正的泛化能力。

zh.title: 复现挑战 | Graph Edit Networks 大部分成立，但有一个扩展性结论站不住
zh.subtitle: 卢布尔雅那大学的复现研究：重写模型、逐一核对四个实验主张，并追问那几个合成 benchmark 到底测出了什么

en.text: Results: three of four claims stand, one falls

The original paper makes four core claims: (i) GEN beats VGAE on all three dynamical graph DGPs; (ii) it reaches near-perfect accuracy on the tree DGPs; (iii) forward passes scale sub-quadratically with graph size; and (iv) backward passes scale linearly. The reproduction confirms the first three and refutes the fourth.

The decisive evidence is the slope of a log-log fit of runtime against graph size (a slope below 2 is sub-quadratic; a slope of 1 is linear). Forward-pass slopes come in clearly below 2, so sub-quadratic scaling holds. But the backward-pass slopes, under both edge-filtering schemes, sit clearly above 1 — that is, super-linear. They remain sub-quadratic, but they are not the linear growth the original paper reported.

en.caption: Figure 3. Runtime versus graph scale (x-axis: node count from 100 to 3k; y-axis: runtime; both log-scaled). The four panels show forward and backward passes under Flexible and Constant edge filtering. The black line is the fitted trend: forward passes stay shallow and sub-quadratic, while backward passes rise noticeably faster — especially Constant.backward (bottom right), whose slope is well above 1, directly contradicting the linear-scaling claim.

Table 1. Slopes of the log-log runtime fit (mean ± standard deviation over 5 repetitions). A slope < 2 is sub-quadratic; = 1 is linear. Forward passes are sub-quadratic; backward passes are all above 1 — super-linear — which refutes the original linear-scaling claim.

en.text: Fidelity of the reproduction: the numbers largely match

On accuracy, the reproduction is reassuring: the vast majority of metrics fall within one standard deviation of the originally reported values. The largest deviation was an increase in VGAE deletion precision and insertion recall on the Edit Cycles task, which did not overturn GEN's overall win. On the tree tasks, Boolean Formulae accuracy is 0.98 ± 0.02, and Peano Addition is a perfect 1.0.

en.caption: Figure 4. A diagnostic δ-boxplot: the y-axis is (reproduction − reported), with the red dashed line at 0 marking perfect agreement. These results are for the Game of Life DGP with the hinge-loss GEN under the stricter risk-estimation protocol and a larger test set. Most boxes hug 0, with deviations within about 0.05 — the reproduction closely tracks the original.

en.text: The authors run two robustness checks. First, they replace the ad-hoc random-graph initialization with the established Erdős–Rényi and Configuration models; every metric moves by less than 0.05. Second, introducing the 100-graph held-out test set shifts scores only slightly, by δ ∈ [−0.1, 0.05]. Both point to the same conclusion: the original results do not hinge on an experimental shortcut.

zh.text: 结果：四个主张，三个成立，一个被推翻
原论文有四个核心主张：(i) GEN 在三个动态图 DGP 上都胜过 VGAE；(ii) 在树结构 DGP 上达到近乎完美的准确率；(iii) 前向传播随图规模呈亚二次（sub-quadratic）扩展；(iv) 反向传播随图规模线性扩展。复现证实了前三个，但推翻了第四个。
关键证据是运行时间随图规模的对数-对数拟合斜率（斜率小于 2 即亚二次，等于 1 即线性）。前向传播的斜率确实明显小于 2，亚二次成立；但反向传播在两种边过滤方案下的斜率都明显大于 1，也就是超线性（super-linear）。它仍然是亚二次的，但绝不是原文所说的线性。

zh.caption: 图3 运行时间与图规模的关系（横轴节点数 100→3k，纵轴运行时间，均为对数刻度）。四个子图分别是 Flexible / Constant 两种边过滤下的前向（forward）与反向（backward）传播。黑线是拟合趋势：前向平缓、亚二次；反向明显更陡，尤其是右下角 Constant.backward，斜率远大于 1，直接否定了「反向传播线性扩展」的说法。
表1 运行时间对数-对数拟合斜率（5 次重复的均值 ± 标准差）。斜率 <2 为亚二次，=1 为线性。行是两种边过滤方案（Flexible / Constant），列是前向（Forward）与反向（Backward）传播。前向亚二次成立；反向全部大于 1，即超线性，推翻原文的线性主张。

zh.text: 复现的保真度：数字基本对得上
在准确性这一面，复现结果整体令人放心：绝大多数指标都落在原文报告值的一个标准差之内。偏差最大的一处，是 VGAE 在 Edit Cycles 任务上的删除精度与插入召回有所上升，但这并没有翻盘 GEN 的整体胜出。树结构任务上，Boolean Formulae 准确率为 0.98 ± 0.02，Peano Addition 更是达到完美的 1.0，两项都与原文报告高度一致。

zh.caption: 图4 诊断用 δ 箱线图：纵轴是「复现值 − 原文报告值」，红色虚线为 0（完全一致）。这是在 Game of Life DGP、hinge-loss 版 GEN、并采用更严格的风险估计协议和更大测试集下得到的。绝大多数箱体都紧贴 0 附近、偏差在 0.05 以内，说明复现与原文高度吻合。

zh.text: 作者还做了两项稳健性检查。其一，把原实验里随手写的随机图初始化换成成熟的 Erdős–Rényi 模型和 Configuration 模型，所有指标变化都在 0.05 以内。其二，引入前面说的 100 张图独立测试集后，分数只轻微下移，偏移量 δ ∈ [−0.1, 0.05]。结论都指向：原文结果并不依赖某个实验捷径。

zh.title: 复现挑战 | Graph Edit Networks 大部分成立，但有一个扩展性结论站不住
zh.subtitle: 卢布尔雅那大学的复现研究：重写模型、逐一核对四个实验主张，并追问那几个合成 benchmark 到底测出了什么

en.text: The sharper question: are these benchmarks actually hard?

The most interesting result is the last diagnostic. When the authors sample from the tree generators to see what sequences they actually produce, they find a problem: the generators overwhelmingly produce trees that cannot be simplified at all. Across more than 300,000 samples, the probability of drawing a simplifiable tree is only 0.13 ± 0.003 for Boolean Formulae and 0.26 ± 0.002 for Peano Addition.

en.caption: Figure 5. Distribution of sampled time-series lengths from the tree DGPs (boolean and peano; rows correspond to a maximum of 3–5 operations). The mass piles up at very short series: a large share of samples have almost no simplification steps to perform. That undercuts how demanding the near-perfect-accuracy tasks really are.

en.text: This puts an asterisk on the tidy 'near-perfect accuracy' numbers on the tree tasks. If most test samples require no simplification in the first place, high accuracy reflects an easy task more than a strongly expressive model. Put differently, the model may be replaying transformations it has already learned rather than generalizing to new ones.

zh.text: 更尖锐的追问：这些 benchmark 真的够难吗
真正有意思的是最后一项诊断。作者去采样这些树结构生成器，看它们到底产出什么样的序列，结果发现一个问题：这些生成器绝大多数时候产出的是根本无法再化简的树。在超过 300,000 次采样中，能采到「可化简树」的概率，Boolean Formulae 只有 0.13 ± 0.003，Peano Addition 也只有 0.26 ± 0.002。

zh.caption: 图5 从树结构 DGP 采样得到的时间序列长度分布（boolean 与 peano，行对应最大操作数 3–5）。可以看到分布严重堆在极短序列一侧：大量样本几乎没有可执行的化简步骤。这意味着「近乎完美准确率」的任务，本身可能就没那么有挑战性。

zh.text: 这一发现给「树任务上近乎完美」的漂亮数字打了个问号：如果大部分测试样本本就无需化简，那高准确率更多反映的是任务偏易，而非模型有多强的表达能力。换句话说，模型可能是在重复它已经学会的变换，而不是在泛化。

en.text: Results: three of four claims stand, one falls

The original paper makes four core claims: (i) GEN beats VGAE on all three dynamical graph DGPs; (ii) it reaches near-perfect accuracy on the tree DGPs; (iii) forward passes scale sub-quadratically with graph size; and (iv) backward passes scale linearly. The reproduction confirms the first three and refutes the fourth.

The decisive evidence is the slope of a log-log fit of runtime against graph size (a slope below 2 is sub-quadratic; a slope of 1 is linear). Forward-pass slopes come in clearly below 2, so sub-quadratic scaling holds. But the backward-pass slopes, under both edge-filtering schemes, sit clearly above 1 — that is, super-linear. They remain sub-quadratic, but they are not the linear growth the original paper reported.

en.caption: Figure 3. Runtime versus graph scale (x-axis: node count from 100 to 3k; y-axis: runtime; both log-scaled). The four panels show forward and backward passes under Flexible and Constant edge filtering. The black line is the fitted trend: forward passes stay shallow and sub-quadratic, while backward passes rise noticeably faster — especially Constant.backward (bottom right), whose slope is well above 1, directly contradicting the linear-scaling claim.

Table 1. Slopes of the log-log runtime fit (mean ± standard deviation over 5 repetitions). A slope < 2 is sub-quadratic; = 1 is linear. Forward passes are sub-quadratic; backward passes are all above 1 — super-linear — which refutes the original linear-scaling claim.

zh.caption: 图4 诊断用 δ 箱线图：纵轴是「复现值 − 原文报告值」，红色虚线为 0（完全一致）。这是在 Game of Life DGP、hinge-loss 版 GEN、并采用更严格的风险估计协议和更大测试集下得到的。绝大多数箱体都紧贴 0 附近、偏差在 0.05 以内，说明复现与原文高度吻合。

zh.text: 复现做了什么：重写代码、写清数据、换一套评测协议

这篇复现的价值不只是「跑一遍看数字对不对」。作者用 Python 重新实现了 GEN，核对代码与原文方法是否一致（过程中还帮原作者修好了一段代码），并把原论文只是一笔带过的五个合成数据生成器（DGP）逐一写清楚。这五个 DGP 分两类：动态图系统 Edit Cycles、Degree Rules、Game of Life，以及树结构动态系统 Boolean Formulae、Peano Addition。扩展性实验则用了 arXiv HEP-Th 引文网络（约 27,700 篇论文），从中用滚动时间窗切出 1554 个子图，节点数 N_G ∈ [100, 2786]。
他们还指出原实验一个隐患：训练和测试可能落在同一批图上，模型有机会在评测时「重逢」训练时见过的变换。为此作者提出一套更严格的风险估计协议，专门留出 100 张图作为独立测试集，并在这套协议下重跑实验。

zh.title: 复现挑战 | Graph Edit Networks 大部分成立，但有一个扩展性结论站不住
zh.subtitle: 卢布尔雅那大学的复现研究：重写模型、逐一核对四个实验主张，并追问那几个合成 benchmark 到底测出了什么

en.text: Fidelity of the reproduction: the numbers largely match

On accuracy, the reproduction is reassuring: the vast majority of metrics fall within one standard deviation of the originally reported values. The largest deviation was an increase in VGAE deletion precision and insertion recall on the Edit Cycles task, which did not overturn GEN's overall win. On the tree tasks, Boolean Formulae accuracy is 0.98 ± 0.02, and Peano Addition is a perfect 1.0.

en.caption: Figure 4. A diagnostic δ-boxplot: the y-axis is (reproduction − reported), with the red dashed line at 0 marking perfect agreement. These results are for the Game of Life DGP with the hinge-loss GEN under the stricter risk-estimation protocol and a larger test set. Most boxes hug 0, with deviations within about 0.05 — the reproduction closely tracks the original.

en.text: The authors run two robustness checks. First, they replace the ad-hoc random-graph initialization with the established Erdős–Rényi and Configuration models; every metric moves by less than 0.05. Second, introducing the 100-graph held-out test set shifts scores only slightly, by δ ∈ [−0.1, 0.05]. Both point to the same conclusion: the original results do not hinge on an experimental shortcut.
Takeaway: elegant and reproducible, but don't overrate its scaling or its difficulty

Taken together, the reproduction offers a measured verdict. GEN is an elegant, interpretable, and genuinely reproducible architecture, and three of the paper's four claims survive independent scrutiny. But the reproduction corrects one scaling claim — backward passes are super-linear, not linear — and it cautions that several of the synthetic benchmarks let the model win by revisiting transitions it has already learned rather than by generalizing.

It is worth noting that the study's careful documentation of the five data generators may be as valuable as its verdict on the claims: anyone reusing these benchmarks benefits directly from it. The authors close with a call for more rigorous, more practically grounded evaluation of an otherwise promising architecture.

zh.text: 在图神经网络（Graph Neural Network, GNN）里，一个不太起眼但很实际的任务是「图的时间序列预测」：给定一个随时间演化的图序列，预测下一时刻的图长什么样。它不是给节点或边打个分那么简单，而是要说清楚从当前图到下一张图，具体发生了哪些结构变化。
标准 GNN 在这里有点力不从心。它们输出的是节点或边的概率分数，而不是「插入一个节点、删掉一条边、给某个顶点改标签」这种能真正把一张图变成下一张图的结构化操作。Graph Edit Network（GEN，图编辑网络）就是为填这个缺口而提出的：它作为 GNN 的输出层，直接预测一段可读的「编辑脚本」。
本文要讲的不是 GEN 原始论文，而是一篇独立复现研究。作者重新实现了 GEN，逐一核对了原文的四个实验主张，并把原论文语焉不详的几个合成数据生成器彻底写清楚。结论是有褒有贬：四个主张里三个站得住，但「反向传播随图规模线性扩展」这一条被推翻了；更尖锐的是，他们发现有几个 benchmark 其实是在奖励模型「记住见过的变换」，而不是真正的泛化能力。

zh.caption: 图1 Edit Cycles 数据生成器产生的三条循环时间序列。每一步的图变换都被写成一段编辑操作 δ（如 ins 插入节点、eins 插入边、del 删除节点），红色箭头即一次「图编辑」。这正是 GEN 要学着预测的目标：不是一张静态图，而是把当前图变成下一张图的那串操作。

zh.text: 论文：https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.6574701 （ReScience C 2022，ML Reproducibility Challenge 2021）
代码：https://github.com/MarusaOrazem/reproducibility_challenge
复现的保真度：数字基本对得上
在准确性这一面，复现结果整体令人放心：绝大多数指标都落在原文报告值的一个标准差之内。偏差最大的一处，是 VGAE 在 Edit Cycles 任务上的删除精度与插入召回有所上升，但这并没有翻盘 GEN 的整体胜出。树结构任务上，Boolean Formulae 准确率为 0.98 ± 0.02，Peano Addition 更是达到完美的 1.0，两项都与原文报告高度一致。

zh.caption: 图4 诊断用 δ 箱线图：纵轴是「复现值 − 原文报告值」，红色虚线为 0（完全一致）。这是在 Game of Life DGP、hinge-loss 版 GEN、并采用更严格的风险估计协议和更大测试集下得到的。绝大多数箱体都紧贴 0 附近、偏差在 0.05 以内，说明复现与原文高度吻合。

zh.text: 作者还做了两项稳健性检查。其一，把原实验里随手写的随机图初始化换成成熟的 Erdős–Rényi 模型和 Configuration 模型，所有指标变化都在 0.05 以内。其二，引入前面说的 100 张图独立测试集后，分数只轻微下移，偏移量 δ ∈ [−0.1, 0.05]。结论都指向：原文结果并不依赖某个实验捷径。
